boundary_rule.tail_start_rule: the tail is every line from the first line whose content, after stripping leading whitespace, starts with 底本： -- mirrors aozora_body_range's `line.trim_start().starts_with("底本：")` check in crates/ab-aozora-aat/src/lib.rs
colophon_heads: 青空文庫作成ファイル：

transitions.when: line (stripped) starts with a provenance_heads entry
line (stripped) starts with a colophon_heads entry

transitions.note: state is left unchanged, not cleared

transitions.when: line is non-blank, matches no head, and state is set
transitions.note: class is terminal_provenance when state is provenance, colophon_metadata when state is colophon

transitions.when: line is non-blank, matches no head, and state is unset

rule_extensions_note: empty: the brief's head-marker skeleton, unmodified, classified every tail line in this run with zero unclassifiable residual (works_unclassifiable == 0) -- no extension beyond 底本：/底本の親本： (provenance) and 入力：/校正：/青空文庫作成ファイル：/※ (colophon) was needed. Lines matching other colophon-shaped prefixes the reference scanner also recognizes (親本：/初出：/校閲：/作成日：/修正：/ファイル作成：) are still classified correctly: they inherit whatever state the block already carries rather than needing their own head entry, since they never open a NEW block by themselves in the corpus.

reference_coverage.reference_mechanism: terminal_provenance_occurrences counts SegmentBoundaryTerminalProvenance markers (crates/ab-source-syntax/src/lib.rs terminal_provenance_note_end): a ［＃地付き］（…） note immediately followed by a 底本： line -- a narrow structural co-occurrence, not 'has a 底本 block'. colophon_metadata_occurrences counts LINES matching a fixed ~20-prefix set including 底本：/底本の親本：/親本：/初出： AND 入力：/校正：/校閲：/作成日：/修正：/ファイル作成：/青空文庫作成ファイル： together in ONE undifferentiated bucket (is_colophon_metadata_line in crates/ab-coverage/src/bin/source_inventory.rs) -- this conflation is exactly what ABC policy v0.2.0 flags needs_measurement_split and what this instrument splits. It is also a pure per-line prefix match with no state: it never counts a bare continuation line (an edition/date line, a plain name).
reference_coverage.this_run_unit: works_scanned/works_with_terminal_provenance/works_with_colophon count corpus TEXT ENTRIES (see works_scanned note above); terminal_provenance_lines/colophon_lines count ALL tail lines under the stateful rule (heads + inherited continuations); head_line_hits counts only the head-line subset (lines literally matching a provenance_heads/colophon_heads prefix) -- the comparable-in-kind figure to the reference's per-line prefix scan, modulo the head-list and prefix-set differences above.

revision_2.reason: Task 15's C4-gate confinement audit found the Task 12 scanner disagreed with the Rust corpus pipeline's ground truth on exactly 6 of 17886 corpus text entries (out of 17886 total). Root cause: this reader used to dispatch zip-vs-plain by filename extension only; the pinned corpus contains files named `*.txt` whose actual bytes are zip archives, and two zip archives whose central directory disagrees with their own local file header. Fixed in reports/source-regions/terminal-provenance-split.py (entry selection now sniffs zip magic bytes by content, matching crates/ab-index/src/index.rs's `is_zip_file`; zip reading now falls back to trusting only the local file header when the central directory is corrupt or unreadable, matching crates/ab-index/src/index.rs and crates/ab-check/src/check.rs's `by_index_raw` + manual decompress, which never cross-checks a central-directory CRC/size). The normative boundary rule itself (reports/lib/terminal_provenance.py's classify_tail state machine, PROVENANCE_HEADS/COLOPHON_HEADS, tail-start marker) is UNCHANGED -- only entry selection/reading changed.

defect_classes.description: Stray/corrupt duplicate file read instead of the real corpus entry: a `.txt`-named file in a `cards/<id>/files/` directory whose actual bytes are a truncated/corrupt zip archive. Extension-based dispatch read its raw zip bytes as Shift_JIS garbage (misclassified no_tail) instead of excluding it, the way the Rust corpus pipeline does (`invalid Zip archive: No CDFH found`, omitted from index.json's 17886-entry universe).
defect_classes.resolution: now correctly excluded (unreadable_entries), matching Rust exactly

defect_classes.description: Same root cause as Class A, but the zip data itself is genuinely valid: a `.txt`-named file in `cards/<id>/files/` whose actual bytes are a fully-formed, decompressible zip archive containing a genuine `底本：` tail. Extension-based dispatch misread it as raw Shift_JIS garbage, missing the real tail entirely (misclassified no_tail).
defect_classes.resolution: now correctly read via content-sniffed zip dispatch; both find a genuine terminal_provenance tail, matching the Rust pipeline's real appended source_note

defect_classes.description: Two zip entries python's stdlib `zipfile` cannot read (one has a central-directory CRC/uncompressed-size that disagrees with its own local file header; one has a central directory/EOCD that is not parseable as a coherent whole at all), which the Rust `zip` crate's `by_index_raw` + manual decompress path reads fine (never cross-checking a central-directory CRC/size against the local header) -- correctly finding no tail on both.
defect_classes.resolution: now correctly read via a local-header-trusting fallback that never validates a central-directory CRC/size; both correctly resolve to no_tail, matching Rust
